grand_strategy.reading:
The internationally recognised government of Yemen is a state held up from outside: legal
seat at the UN, salaries and grants from Riyadh, air power largely Saudi, and most of its people
beyond its writ. Its grand strategy is therefore less a plan than a position in a Saudi
plan, and Luttwak's levels diverge sharply. At the theatre level the goal is the
Houthis' defeat (the PLC's own word is the 'decisive phase', 4 Oct 2026); at the
grand-strategic level the goal is to remain the party Riyadh must keep, against a
Houthi movement that Riyadh has negotiated with since 2022 and against an Emirati
network it destroyed in January 2026. The 2026 sequence is the paradox of the card:
the elimination of the STC bought Saudi control of the south and left the camp
without its best money and units, then the coast fell within a week; the Iran war
turned the Bab al-Mandab into a bargaining chip, so that the contest over Yemen's
coast is settled in Tehran, Riyadh, Washington and Muscat as much as in Taiz and
Mokha. What decides the next year is Saudi stamina and Saudi pain: the government
needs the offensive to continue and cannot control the price Riyadh pays. Signals
that are not rows: the Houthis' own account of their aims (Sanaa-based media only,
not researched); the Southern movement after the STC's formal dissolution, which
appears in the sources only as protest and bombings; the UAE's silence on Yemen
since January except for condemning the strikes on Saudi airports.

stances.note: Mirrors Saudi Arabia's own card (ally, same sources). De facto alliance rather than a treaty: the coalition has fought for the government since 26 Mar 2015, Riyadh pays salaries and grants (USD 347m budget grant, USD 90m salary package, USD 507m for projects in 2026), sponsors the units Abu Dhabi used to fund, and its aircraft cover the offensive of 4 Oct 2026, which al-Alimi called the work of 'a true partner'. Friction exists - Riyadh set a budget as a condition of aid, the 2023 roadmap came out of direct Saudi-Houthi talks, and the Sana'a Center asks Riyadh to act as partner rather than patron and to avoid indiscriminate air strikes - but it is voiced by analysts, not by the government, whose line is thanks; the structure is alliance, not `reluctant_ally`. Warming because Riyadh now owns the anti-Houthi side outright. Bond - affinity: neighbours with tribal and border ties (our reading).
